### To study at UNSW, you may be required to provide evidence that your English language ability meets our requirements.

###### You may need to submit results from an acceptable English language test taken in the last two years prior to starting at UNSW.

##### Here are some ways you can achieve the language requirements:

- English Tests











UNSW accepts a number of English language qualifications to meet our English language requirements provided:



  - You completed the test no more than two years before your intended start date, the English test must be dated on or after the 1st of January (two years prior) for Term 1 commencement, 1st of May for Term 2  commencement or the 1st of August (two years prior) for Term 3 commencement and
  - You achieved the minimum scores for your desired program.

###### List of test we accept:

1. IELTS (International English Language Testing System) - Academic version, IELTS One Skill Retake and IELTS UKVI only. Online version is not accepted
2. TOEFL iBT (Test of English as a Foreign Language - internet-based), including TOEFL iBT Home Edition (TOEFL for Australia version only)

3. PTE (Pearson Test of English - Academic)
4. C1 Advanced Cambridge (formerly known as CAE - Cambridge Advanced English)
5. C2 Proficiency Cambridge (formerly known CPE - Cambridge Proficiency English)
6. ANU Access Program

###### List of test we accept from Term 1, 2027 onwards:

1. LanguageCert Academic
2. MET (Michigan English Test)


Check below to see if your results meet our English language requirements.

  - IELTS (International English Language Testing System) – Academic version, IELTS One Skill Retake and IELTS UKVI only. Online version is not accepted












    Note: When applying for a cross-faculty double degree, the higher English requirements apply.



    IELTS One Skill Retake allows test taker to retake any one component of the IELTS test (Listening, Reading, Writing or Speaking) without redoing all four sections in case they have missed the required score. Test takers are eligible to book IELTS One Skill Retake after they recently completed a full test on a computer and received their IELTS test score, from an eligible test centre. To be eligible, you must book your IELTS One Skill Retake within 60 days of the original test date and you can take only one retake for each full IELTS test. Your result will be valid for two years from the original test date which you can find on your Test Report Form.

  - LanguageCert Academic












    Note: When applying for a cross-faculty double degree, the higher English requirements apply.


    LanguageCert Academic is accepted as a four-skill English language test for admission purposes at UNSW. This test can be used for applications from Term 1, 2027 onwards. Applicants must complete the test at an approved test centre, as results obtained through remote-proctored or at-home formats are not accepted. In addition, test results must be valid at the time of program commencement and therefore must have been issued within two years, unless otherwise specified under UNSW policy.

- UNSW College English Course











If you have received a Conditional Offer from UNSW Sydney, you can meet our English language requirements by taking UNSW College’s [University English Entry Course (UEEC)](https://www.unswcollege.edu.au/study/university-english-entry-course) and achieving the minimum scores as outlined below by course. However, if you wish to apply for a cross-faculty double degree, there will be higher English language requirements to meet. Please note the course must be completed no more than two years before your intended start date.



[UNSW College, opens in a new window](https://www.unswcollege.edu.au/) offers university pathway programs that provide a seamless transition to UNSW Sydney so you can achieve your academic and career goals. They will provide you with the academic and English language foundations for success. [Contact UNSW College, opens in a new window](https://www.unswcollege.edu.au/contact-us/) to find out more.

- Prior Study











UNSW accepts prior study results to meet our English language requirements on certain conditions.



UNSW accepts prior studies completed in English to meet our English language requirements depending on whether you are from an English-speaking background or non-English speaking background.



English-speaking background:



  - Citizens of English-speaking countries, or
  - Permanent Residents of English-speaking countries, or
  - Minimum of ten years in an English-speaking country and completed secondary or tertiary education in an English-speaking country.

  - Senior Secondary Studies







    Senior Secondary qualifications from a recognised [English-speaking country](https://www.unsw.edu.au/study/how-to-apply/english-language-requirements#thingstoknow) will meet our English language requirements if they were:



    - taught and examined in English
    - attempted no more than two years before your intended start date if you are from a non-English speaking background.

Applicants who completed the **GCE A Levels through a UK examining board (eg. CIE, Pearson/Edexcel)** in non-English speaking countries must meet the following criteria:

    - a minimum Grade C\* in one of the following approved essay-based A Level subjects:
      - English Language,
      - English Literature,
      - English Language and Literature, or
      - a Humanities subject, such as Sociology, History, Law, or Psychology

_\\* NOTE_: **The following programs require a minimum Grade A** in one of approved essay-based subjects listed above:

    - B Education (all programs)
    - B Social Work (Honours), including all its joint programs
    - All Law and Business undergraduate programs (except B Criminology and Criminal Justice)
    - B Nutrition/M Dietetics & Food Innovation
    - B Medical Studies/Doctor of Medicine
    - B Exercise Sciene/M Physiotherapy & Exercise Physiology
    - B Pharmaceutical Medicine/M Pharmacy
    - B Applied Exercise Science/M Clinical Exercise Physiology

    Qualifications from Germany, Hong Kong, India, Malaysia, Switzerland will meet our English language requirements provided they were:



    - completed no more than two years before your intended start date, and
    - meet the minimum scores for your desired course.

  - Post-Secondary and Tertiary Qualifications in English attempted or completed







    UNSW accepts completed or incomplete post-secondary or tertiary qualifications\* completed in English to meet our English language requirements depending on whether you are from an English-speaking background or non-English speaking background.



    English-speaking background:



    - Citizens of English-speaking countries, or
    - Permanent Residents of English-speaking countries, or
    - Minimum of ten years in an English-speaking country and completed secondary or tertiary education in an English-speaking country.

_Note:_

    - _Upon completion of Bachelor of Education programs (Primary & Secondary) and Master of Teaching programs (Primary & Secondary), you must comply with the [NESA English Language Proficiency Requirements](https://educationstandards.nsw.edu.au/wps/portal/nesa/home) and provide the necessary evidence when you apply for provisional and conditional accreditation._
    - _For Master of Clinical Neuropsychology and Master of Psychology (Clinical & Forensic) including combined PhD/Master please refer to [AHPRA](https://www.ahpra.gov.au/Registration/Registration-Standards/English-language-skills.aspx) website for pathways that you can use to demonstrate your English competence._

###### COMPLETED QUALIFICATION

If you are from an English-speaking background, you will meet our English language requirements if your qualification was:

    - an AQF Diploma or higher from a recognised institution in an English-speaking country or
    - from an institution listed in the World Higher Education Database ( [WHED](https://www.whed.net/home.php "https://www.whed.net/home.php")) with English clearly stated as the sole language of instruction.

Please provide:

    - official academic transcript
    - proof of citizenship or residency.

If you are from a non-English-speaking background, you will meet our English language requirements if your qualification was:

    - an AQF Bachelor or higher from a recognised institution in an English-speaking country, or
    - from an institution listed in the World Higher Education Database ( [WHED](https://www.whed.net/home.php "https://www.whed.net/home.php")) with English clearly stated as the sole language of instruction
    - completed within the five years before you start your degree at UNSW.

If you are from a non-English-speaking background, you will meet our English language requirements if your qualification was:

    - an AQF Diploma, Advanced Diploma or Associate Degree from a recognised institution in an English-speaking country, or
    - from an institution listed in the World Higher Education Database ( [WHED](https://www.whed.net/home.php "https://www.whed.net/home.php")) with English clearly stated as the sole language of instruction
    - gained within the two years before you start your degree at UNSW.

For programs that are jointly delivered by two institutions, leading to one or more qualifications, please provide:

    - official academic transcript and
    - official statement or certificate from the Registrar (or equivalent) confirming English as the sole language of instruction and assessment, issued on official letterhead and provided in original form.

###### INCOMPLETE QUALIFICATION

If you are from an English-speaking background, you will meet our English language requirements if:

    - You have completed at least one year of full-time equivalent study at an AQF Bachelor or higher from a recognised institution from a recognised institution in an English speaking country, or
    - from an institution listed in the World Higher Education Database ( [WHED](https://www.whed.net/home.php "https://www.whed.net/home.php")) with English clearly stated as the sole language of instruction.

Please provide:

    - official academic transcript
    - proof of citizenship or residency.

If you are from a non English-speaking background, you will meet our English language requirements if:

    - You have completed at least one year of full-time equivalent study at an AQF Bachelor or higher from a recognised institution in an English speaking country, or
    - from an institution listed in the World Higher Education Database ( [WHED](https://www.whed.net/home.php "https://www.whed.net/home.php")) with English clearly stated as the sole language of instruction.
    - And completed within the two years before you start your degree at UNSW.

- English Waiver











##### What is an English waiver?



An English waiver is a decision by UNSW to waive the English language requirements based on life experience and circumstances. To apply for an English waiver you will need to meet any two of the conditions listed below.





##### How can I apply for an English waiver?



  - You can apply for an English Waiver during your online application – just submit a personal statement with your supporting documentation under the English Language Requirements section of the online application form.

  - If you are applying for an undergraduate and postgraduate course, you can apply for an English waiver by submitting an enquiry [here](https://www.enquiry.unsw.edu.au/).
  - If you are applying for a higher degree by research, you need to upload your request and supporting documents to the [UNSW Applicant Portal](https://apply.unsw.edu.au/). Completed English waiver requests must be submitted no less than 8 weeks prior to the relevant [deadline](https://www.unsw.edu.au/research/hdr/application#panel-3).

##### Is my country recognised as an English-speaking country?

UNSW recognises the following countries as English-speaking: American Samoa, Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Botswana, Canada, Fiji, Gibraltar, Ghana, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Papua New Guinea, Singapore, Solomon Islands, South Africa, The Gambia, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, United Kingdom (including Northern Ireland), United States of America, Zambia, Zimbabwe.

##### Does UNSW accept all requests for an English waiver?

  - UNSW does not accept any requests for an English waiver for the Graduate Diploma in Psychology, Master of Psychology (including combined PhD/Master), Master of Clinical Neuropsychology, Bachelor of Education (Primary & Secondary), Master of Teaching (Primary and Secondary) or Bachelor of Aviation (Flying).

  - UNSW Canberra does not accept any requests for an English waiver for Higher Degree Research program including the Doctor of Philosophy, Professional Doctorates, Master by Research or Master of Philosophy.

| Master of Teaching (Primary and Secondary) and Bachelor of Education (all programs) | English waivers are not available for admission to the Master of Teaching (Primary and Secondary) and Bachelor of Education (all programs) |
| Master of Psychology (Clinical & Forensic) including combined PhD/Master | English waivers are not available for admission to the Master of Psychology (including combined PhD/Master) |
| Master of Clinical Neuro-psychology | English waivers are not available for admission to the Master of Clinical Neuropsychology |
| Graduate Diploma in Psychology | English waivers are not available for admission to the Graduate Diploma in Psychology |

  - Directly relevant work experience







    **Directly relevant Work Experience for at least the last two years – any program**



    You have at least two years of directly relevant work experience, in the relevant industry or equivalent discipline practice, in an [English-speaking country](https://www.international.unsw.edu.au/english-language-requirements?field_english_language_tid=4026) or workplace where the sole language of business was English.



    Please provide:



    - A letter from your employer on company letterhead which states your position title, the duties you undertook and an idea of what level of English was spoken and how English was used in terms of written or verbal communication.

**Directly relevant Work Experience for at least five years out of the last seven – AGSM @ UNSW program only**

You have five years, out of the last seven, of directly relevant work experience, in the relevant industry or equivalent discipline practice, in an [English-speaking country](https://www.international.unsw.edu.au/english-language-requirements?field_english_language_tid=4026) or workplace where the sole language of business was English.

Please provide a letter from your employer on company letterhead for any employment which is not already covered by the referee letters you have already submitted with your AGSM application.

Please provide:

    - A letter from your employer on company letterhead which states your position title, the duties you undertook and an idea of what level of English was spoken and how English was used in terms of written or verbal communication.

If you can demonstrate this experience, you will not need to satisfy a second condition for an English waiver.

  - Successful prior study for a minimum of one year full-time completed in English between two and five years ago







    You successfully completed at least one year of full-time study, in an assessable qualification, at a university or other post-secondary educational institution in an English-speaking country or from an institution listed in the World Higher Education Database ( [WHED](https://www.whed.net/home.php)) with English clearly stated as the sole language of instruction.



    Please provide:



    - Official academic transcript and
    - Official statement or certificate from the Registrar (or equivalent) confirming English as the sole language of instruction and assessment, issued on official letter head and provided in original form.

  - Residency in an English-speaking country for at least five years







    You lived in a recognised [English-speaking country](https://www.international.unsw.edu.au/english-language-requirements?field_english_language_tid=4026) for at least five years before you plan to start your course at UNSW.



    Please provide:



    - References which state whether a basic, medium, high or academic level of English speaking and writing skills was needed.
    - Copies of passports and/or visas to prove your residency in the [English-speaking country](https://www.international.unsw.edu.au/english-language-requirements?field_english_language_tid=4026) was for at least five years.

  - NAATI - National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters







    You hold a current valid NAATI accreditation as a Professional Interpreter or Translator, formerly known as Level 3 accredited.



    Please provide:



    - Your certificate of NAATI accreditation.

  - GMAT - Graduate Management Admissions Test - for AGSM @ UNSW







    You sat the GMAT within the last five years and you scored a minimum overall GMAT score of 550 with a minimum score of 25 in Verbal, 35 in Quantitative and 4.0 in the Analytical Writing Assessment (AWA).



    Please provide:



    - Your test results.

  - Doctor/health professional qualified outside Australia and registered with the Medical Board of Australia







    You are a qualified doctor/health professional overseas, hold a current registration with the Medical Board of Australia and are currently employed in the health system in Australia.



    Please provide:



    - Your CV with referees.
    - Proof of your current registration with the Medical Board of Australia.

  - Successful completion of a UNSW Study Abroad or Exchange program within the last two years







    You can supply evidence of successfully completing a UNSW Study Abroad or Exchange program within the last two years.



    Please provide:



    - Your transcript.

  - Successful completion of a recognised Articulation Pathway within the last two years







    You can supply evidence of successfully completing a program within the last two years, which is recognised by UNSW as a defined qualification pathway.



    Please provide:



    - Your transcript.

### Study Abroad & Exchange students

To ensure students have the best possible experience at UNSW and to maximise their chances of personal and academic success, all students including exchange and study abroad students need to meet our English language requirements.  You can view the list of English-speaking countries [here, opens in a new window](https://www.unsw.edu.au/study/how-to-apply/english-language-requirements#thingstoknow).

If English isn't your first language you will need to provide proof of English proficiency at time of application and you can do this by providing evidence that you meet one of UNSW’s approved criteria. You should upload your supporting documents to your Study Abroad or Exchange application.  English proficiency is an entry requirement and we cannot accept students without it.

Here are some ways you can achieve the language requirements.  We recommend you also review the full list of English Language options above.  No other tests or options can be accepted.

- English Language Test Scores







UNSW accepts English language test scores to meet our English language requirements provided:



  - You have completed the test no more than two years before your intended start date, and

  - You achieve the minimum scores for the Study Abroad and Exchange program.  Study Abroad and Exchange students are only required to meet the overall score for IELTS and TOEFL.  You do not need to meet each of the subtests as per a full degree student.

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| **IELTS Academic version only** | **TOEFL Internet-based Test (iBT)** |
| 6.5 overall | 90 overall |

  - **IELTS Academic version only**



    6.5 overall



    **TOEFL Internet-based Test (iBT)**



    90 overall


You should register for your English language test early to avoid delays.

Please note: TOEFL MyBest scores is not a recognised or accepted language test.  The Department of Home Affairs has advised that results from multiple tests cannot be used for meeting English Language proficiency requirements for a student visa.

- Senior Secondary Qualifications







Senior Secondary qualifications from a recognised [English-speaking country](https://www.unsw.edu.au/study/how-to-apply/english-language-requirements#thingstoknow) will meet our English language requirements if they were:



  - taught and examined in English
  - attempted no more than two years before your intended start date if you are from a non-English speaking background.

| All India Senior School Certificate (CBSE) (Standard 12) | - Grade of C1 in English Core |
| Indian School Certificate (ICS) | - 70% in English |

- Post-Secondary or Tertiary Qualifications in English







If you are from an English-speaking background, you will meet our English language requirements if:



  - You have completed at least one year of full-time equivalent study at an AQF Bachelor or higher from a recognised institution, where the program was taught and examined in an English-speaking country or where English is the institution's sole medium of instruction.

Please provide:

  - official academic transcript
  - proof of citizenship or residency.

If you are from a non English-speaking background, you will meet our English language requirements if:

  - You have completed at least one year of full-time equivalent study at an AQF Bachelor or higher from a recognised institution in an English speaking country, or
  - Taught and examined in an English-speaking country or where English is the institution's sole medium of instruction,
  - And the study must have been completed no more than **two years** prior to the commencement of your Study Abroad or Exchange program at UNSW.

- University English Entry Course (UEEC)







If you don’t quite meet the UNSW English language requirements, you may wish to consider undertaking English language study through the UNSW College [University English Entry Course (UEEC)](https://www.unswcollege.edu.au/study/university-english-entry-course) program. You can apply to UEEC to undertake English language study prior to your study abroad or exchange.  You will be provided with a conditional study abroad or exchange offer and you can demonstrate you meet our English language requirements by taking the UEEC program and achieving the minimum grade of C+ and C in writing.  You are responsible for paying any tuition fees directly to UEEC.


### Things to know

- List of Recognised English Speaking Countries







UNSW recognises the following countries as English-speaking: American Samoa, Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Botswana, Canada, Fiji, Gibraltar, Ghana, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Papua New Guinea, Singapore, Solomon Islands, South Africa, The Gambia, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, United Kingdom (including Northern Ireland), United States of America, Zambia, Zimbabwe.

- Conditional Offers







If your application does not meet our English language requirements, but you are otherwise eligible for admission to your desired course, you will be issued a Conditional Letter of Offer.



A full Offer for admission will be issued when you submit documents which demonstrate that you meet our English language requirements.



Conditional Offers based on English language requirements are not offered to UAC applicants for domestic undergraduate or postgraduate coursework programs and any Higher Degree Research applicants.

- Conditional Package Offers







[UNSW College, opens in a new window](https://www.unswcollege.edu.au/) has university pathway programs that provide a seamless transition to UNSW Sydney so you can achieve your academic and career goals including the University English Entry Course.



With a Conditional Package Offer, you will be able to apply for a student visa for the duration of UNSW College’s University English Entry Course (UEEC) and your UNSW course.



The package offer is only valid for UNSW College’s UEEC and this depends on whether you are accepted into the UNSW College.



Conditional package offers are not offered for entry to the Bachelor of Education (any program), Graduate Diploma in Psychology, Master of Psychology (including combined PhD/Master) or Master of Teaching (Primary and Secondary).

- Visa Requirements for International Applicants







For advice on applying for a student visa, [visit the Department of Home Affairs](https://www.homeaffairs.gov.au/).
